Red River County, Texas Tax Sales

Red River County, Texas, conducts tax sales to address unpaid property taxes while offering opportunities for buyers to acquire properties. The process is structured to ensure fairness and transparency for all participants. Below is a clear guide to how tax sales are conducted in Red River County.

Schedule of Sales

Tax sales in Red River County typically take place on the first Tuesday of the month, between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Auctions are held at the East Door of the Red River County Courthouse, located at 200 North Walnut Street, Clarksville, TX. Participants should verify the dates and times by checking public notices or the county website.

Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

Notification and Public Notices

The county issues public notices to inform property owners and potential bidders about upcoming tax sales. These notices are published at least 21 days before the auction and provide important details such as:

  1. The date, time, and location of the auction.
  2. A description of the properties being sold.
  3. The minimum bid amounts, which cover delinquent taxes, penalties, and fees.

The courthouse displays notices and makes them available online for easy access

Registration Requirements

To participate in a tax sale, bidders must register before the auction. The registration process generally includes:

  • Providing valid government-issued identification.

  • Completing any required forms provided by the Red River County Tax Office.

  • Ensuring that the bidder has no delinquent taxes owed in Red River County.

  • Complete registration well in advance to avoid delays on auction day

Preparing for the Auction

Proper preparation is essential for success at a tax sale. Bidders should:

  1. Review the public notices to identify properties of interest.
  2. Research property details, including location, condition, and legal status.
  3. Check for liens or encumbrances that may affect ownership.
  4. Consult with legal or real estate professionals to understand responsibilities and potential risks.
  5. Visit the properties, if possible, to assess their condition and value.

Auction Day Process

The auction process in Red River County is straightforward and follows these steps:

  1. The auctioneer starts bidding at the minimum amount and sells the property to the highest bidder.
  2. Successful bidders must pay immediately. Accepted payment methods typically include cash or cashier’s checks.
  3. The auctioneer announces rules and updates before bidding begins. Participants should arrive early to review these details.

Post-Auction Responsibilities

After successfully purchasing a property, buyers must:

  • Record the deed with the Red River County Clerk’s office to establish ownership.

  • Address any legal or title issues, such as liens or encumbrances.

  • Ensure timely payment of future property taxes to maintain good standing.

Buyers accept full responsibility for the property’s condition and any associated liabilities when purchasing properties “as-is”.

Redemption Period

Texas law provides a redemption period for previous property owners to reclaim their property. The duration depends on the type of property:

  • Homestead and agricultural properties have a two-year redemption period.

  • All other properties have a 180-day redemption period.

To redeem, the former owner must pay the purchase price, recording fees, any taxes paid by the buyer, and a premium. The premium increases to 25% when the property is redeemed within the first year and 50% in the second year for applicable properties.
